record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Sample efficiency of morphological layers for Gestalt-like tasks
record.original_question: Do deep networks that integrate morphological layers require fewer training examples than standard deep-learning architectures when learning Gestalt-pattern-theory-inspired visual concepts such as shape or symmetry?

evidence.quote: Are networks integrating morphological layers more ‘intelligent’ (i.e., requires less training samples) than standard deep learning architectures to learn tasks inspired from Gestalt pattern theory?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of deep neural networks built from standard layers (e.g., convolutional, fully connected, pooling, and normalization layers, together with the usual pointwise nonlinearities) and the class of deep neural networks that, in addition to such layers, also incorporate morphological layers. Here a morphological layer is a trainable nonlinear layer implementing operations from mathematical morphology over images, such as grey-scale dilations and erosions with learnable flat or non-flat structuring elements, defined respectively by

  (f ⊕ b)(x) = sup_{y} { f(x − y) + b(y) },   (f ⊖ b)(x) = inf_{y} { f(x + y) − b(y) },

and compositions thereof (openings, closings, top-hats, etc.), where b is the learnable structuring function.

Fix a family T of supervised visual learning tasks inspired by Gestalt pattern theory, i.e., tasks whose target concepts are global perceptual organization properties such as shape category, closure, good continuation, or bilateral/rotational symmetry of binary or grey-scale patterns. For an architecture A and task t ∈ T, let N(A, t, ε) denote the minimal number of i.i.d. training samples needed for A, trained by an admissible optimization procedure, to achieve generalization error at most ε on t.

Question: Is it the case that, for every Gestalt-inspired task t ∈ T and every sufficiently small ε > 0, there exists a morphology-augmented architecture A_morph and a standard architecture A_std (of comparable capacity) such that

  N(A_morph, t, ε)  <  N(A_std, t, ε),

with the gap being non-negligible? Equivalently, do deep networks that integrate morphological layers require strictly fewer training examples than purely standard deep architectures when learning Gestalt-pattern-theory-inspired visual concepts such as shape or symmetry?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works show that morphological layers can improve accuracy on shape-related image datasets and that exploiting symmetry priors generally improves sample efficiency, but no study directly establishes that morphology-augmented networks systematically require fewer training samples than standard deep architectures on Gestalt-pattern-theory tasks. Evidence on whether convolutional networks even exhibit Gestalt grouping is mixed. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Deep Morphological Neural Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Morphological layers outperform convolutional layers on datasets closely related to shape features such as GTSRB.
status_evidence.claim: Morphological layers improve accuracy on shape-related tasks, but sample efficiency on Gestalt tasks is not directly addressed.

status_evidence.title: Mixed Evidence for Gestalt Grouping in Deep Neural Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Convolutional networks were sensitive in a human-like fashion to some Gestalt principles only at the output layer.
status_evidence.claim: Whether deep networks capture Gestalt principles at all is still contested, indicating the comparative sample-efficiency question is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Morphological symmetries in robot learning
status_evidence.snippet: Exploiting morphological symmetries offers improved sample efficiency and generalization.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetry priors are known to improve sample efficiency in general, but this does not specifically resolve the question for morphological image-processing layers on Gestalt tasks.
